messages.subject: Assistance Needed with Seasonality Modelling in INLA
parts:
Hello INLA Community,

I am reaching out to seek assistance in properly framing a seasonality model using INLA. I am relatively new to this framework and am eager to learn. While I have found various online resources, I am struggling with understanding the implementation of a seasonality model.

I have referred to INLA::inla.doc("seasonal") and reviewed discussions such as this thread  https://groups.google.com/g/r-inla-discussion-group/c/31_a_RcBC-U, but I still find some aspects unclear.

Model Description:

I am working with a dataset consisting of monthly records indicating the presence or absence of an event, along with relevant variables. I have gaps in the time series, meaning that my data cover just a few random months every year.  The data includes repeated measures at each location, which are not spatially correlated. Each location is uniquely identified by a code. Here is a sample of my data:

 

  time_step Month  Year Region Country smllcnt Place     Code           Y tmean_lag0

      <int> <int> <int> <chr>  <chr>     <int> <chr>     <chr>      <dbl>      <dbl>

       201     3  2023 Africa Réunion       1 Réunion   REU            0       297.

       67     1  2012 Europe Germany       0 Ahrweiler DEU.11.1_1     0       276.

       69     3  2012 Europe Germany       0 Ahrweiler DEU.11.1_1     0       281.

      94     4  2014 Europe Germany       0 Ahrweiler DEU.11.1_1     0       284.

       96     6  2014 Europe Germany       0 Ahrweiler DEU.11.1_1     0       288.

      116     2  2016 Europe Germany       0 Ahrweiler DEU.11.1_1     0       276.

I aim to construct a binomial model that accounts for seasonality and includes random effects for location. To address seasonality despite gaps, I created a "time_step" index spanning all months and years from the earliest to the latest date. This index starts at 1 (2006-07-01) and ends at 210 (2023-12-01).

 

Model Structure:

Here is my attempt at coding this in R using INLA:

baseformula = Y ~ 1 + f(Code, model = "iid") + f(time_step, model = "seasonal", season.length = 12)

 

res = inla(baseformula, family = 'binomial', data = data,

           Ntrials = 1,

           control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),

           control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, return.marginals.predictor = TRUE))

 Questions:

·         Is this the proper way to include seasonality in my model?

·         How can I validate the seasonal assumption?

·         Will this approach allow me to make predictions for missing and future time steps?

I would greatly appreciate any guidance or suggestions. Thank you!

 

Best regards,
